articles.title: World: Attacks on humanitarian workers surge under new armed conflict tactics, leaving children without life‐saving aid
articles.description: Countries: World, Sudan, Ukraine Source: World Vision Ahead of World Humanitarian Day, World Vision calls for greater protection and accountability as new conflict tactics threaten aid workers, humanitarian access and children's survival. London/Geneva, 10 August 2026 - A child should not have to know the sound of a military drone. Yet for millions of children living through conflict, the buzz overhead has become as familiar as a school bell. Drones can now be heard above hospitals in Sudan, over war-torn villages in Ukraine, along roads where aid convoys once moved, and near shelters, where children wait for food, medicine, clean water, and safety. Their presence signals danger, causing panic and keeping families indoors. Drone threats close roads, empty clinics and prevent aid workers from reaching those who need assistance most. This World Humanitarian Day, World Vision warns that humanitarian access, protection of civilians, and aid worker safety are being reshaped by the changing nature of conflict, including the growing use of drones and other emerging technologies, leaving children cut off from the help they need most. In East Darfur, Sudan, a drone attack on Ed-Dain Teaching Hospital reportedly killed at least 64 people , including 13 children and healthcare workers , and left 90 others severely injured . The hospital was rendered completely non-functional, cutting off life-saving healthcare services. Drone attacks are being reported across a widening area of Sudan , including UN-reported strikes in El Obeid that hit a power and fuel station, forcing medical facilities to close. In Ukraine, families describe children hiding in basements, listening to drones above their villages . Some have been separated from their parents for months while seeking safety abroad. "Technology may be changing how conflicts are fought but it cannot change our responsibility to protect human life and dignity. Every drone strike that closes a clinic, destroys a road or forces aid workers to turn back is also an attack on a child’s chance to survive. Humanitarian workers are not targets. Hospitals are not targets. Children are not collateral damage,” said Isabel Gomes, Global Lead, Disaster Management, World Vision International. More than 1,000 humanitarian workers have been killed in the past three years , with 350 killed in 2025 alone , the second-highest number ever recorded. At the same time, the Global Coalition to Protect Education from Attack recorded at least 8,566 attacks on education in 2024 and 2025 , more than a 40 per cent increase compared with 2022–2023, while the World Health Organization has verified more than 2000 attacks on healthcare facilities, personnel and services in 2026. When aid workers are attacked or blocked from reaching people in need, children are left waiting for food, medicine and protection that may never come. Too often, those risking their lives to help are local people and members of the very communities caught in the conflict. Last year, World Vision welcomed the " Declaration for the Protection of Humanitarian Personnel ", a commitment to uphold international law and take practical steps to protect humanitarian personnel. This was an important step towards safeguarding aid workers, defending humanitarian access, and strengthening accountability when those protections are violated. This World Humanitarian Day, World Vision calls on governments and parties to conflict to: Protect humanitarian workers, civilians, and civilian infrastructure in line with international humanitarian law. Guarantee safe, sustained, and unimpeded humanitarian access for children and families affected by conflict. Ensure independent investigations, accountability, and consequences for attacks on humanitarian workers, healthcare facilities, and other civilian infrastructure. Address the humanitarian consequences of drones and other emerging military technologies, including their impact on humanitarian access, civilian protection, and children’s safety. Protecting humanitarian workers is inseparable from protecting children. Every attack that prevents aid workers from reaching a community exposes children to hunger, disease, violence, exploitation, and despair. “When humanitarian workers are attacked or prevented from reaching communities, children lose the people bringing food, medicine, clean water and protection. Governments must treat every such attack not simply as another statistic, but as a test of whether international law will be upheld,” said Gomes. This World Humanitarian Day, the global #ActForHumanity campaign reminds us that every humanitarian worker killed is more than a number. It forces us to ask uncomfortable questions: How many more aid workers must die, how many more hospitals stop functioning, before expressions of concern are matched by accountability? Protection requires action, accountability, and consequences when international law is violated. World Vision honours humanitarian workers who have lost their lives and those who continue to serve in the world’s most dangerous places. Remembrance must now be matched by protection, access, and accountability. Notes to editors World Humanitarian Day is marked annually on 19 August. The 2026 campaign, #ActForHumanity , calls for stronger protection of humanitarian workers, accountability for attacks and safe humanitarian access for people in crisis. For more information, please contact: Annila Harris Sr Advisor Humanitarian Communications and Engagement Email: annila_harris@wvi.org Learn more about protecting those who protect children https://www.wvi.org/world-humanitarian-day About World Vision World Vision is a Christian humanitarian organisation dedicated to working with children, families and their communities to reach their full potential by tackling the root causes of poverty and injustice. World Vision serves all people, regardless of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. For more information, please visit www.wvi.org

articles.title: 'Dubious' new White House counsel pick reveals Trump's real scheme: attorney
articles.description: President Donald Trump's incoming White House counsel reveals the role that the president's top lawyers are meant to have, a legal analyst explained. On a Tuesday episode of her podcast, attorney and journalist Katie Phang unloaded on Will Scharf , who's currently serving as staff secretary but is set to take over as the White House counsel on September 1. She described Scharf as having "had a history of being a little bit dubious" as Trump's former personal lawyer. "The only qualification you need is not competency. It is not loyalty to the United States Constitution," Phang said. "It's the capacity to only kiss one person's a—, and that is convicted felon, Donald Trump." He's the latest Trump personal lawyer to be awarded a job close to the president, following the confirmation of Attorney General Todd Blanche . Phang noted that Emil Bove , a judge on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 3rd Circuit, U.S. Attorney Lindsey Halligan, and Solicitor General John Sauer were also in Trump's personal legal orbit before they "garnered some cushy positions." Scharf's new job as Trump's White House counsel will involve "running a team of lawyers and advisers who are going to be telling felon Trump whether he is running afoul of the law or not," according to Phang. "And of course, we all laugh and chuckle when we hear that because it is a day ending in Y when felon Trump runs afoul of the law," Phang explained. "The dangers here with constantly having personal lawyers as your attorney general, as federal appellate judges, as your White House counsel, as your solicitor general...they're going to sit there and scheme and strategize a way to try and end-run the law." She pointed out that the Trump administration's record of winning and losing cases in court is "pretty abysmal," but the real damage comes with "the havoc they wreak along the way. It is the destruction of values, norms, rule of law, and institutions." After all that destruction, Phang warned, "It's the rebuild that we're left with, that we're stuck with when these a— are out of power."

articles.title: DOJ quietly issues opinion with ‘big implications’ for keeping Trump talks secret: report
articles.description: The Justice Department quietly released a memo Monday that could have “big implications” for Democrats seeking to hold President Donald Trump accountable should they retake control of Congress in the midterms, Punchbowl News founder Jake Sharman warned Tuesday. The memo, issued by the DOJ's Office of Legal Counsel, asserts that the president has the legal right to withhold his communications with "private advisers," even when Congress requests them through legal channels, so long as “they relate to official presidential decisionmaking.” “[The opinion] extends to ‘direct advisors’ communication with outside advisers,” Sharman wrote Tuesday in a social media post on X. “Big implications if Dems take back the House and start investigating Trump.” Punchbowl News noted in its Tuesday morning newsletter that the DOJ's position would effectively block congressional inquiries into Trump's communications, which could be key to Democrats' efforts to probe his business and other dealings. “That would let any president – including President Donald Trump – wall off a broad swath of communication from congressional scrutiny,” Punchbowl News’ report reads. “It lands as Democrats look increasingly likely to win back the House – and subpoena power.” House Democrats have already been advancing a plan to “hold Trump accountable” should they have a strong showing in the midterms, one that relies on probing Trump-linked businesses. The DOJ's new memo could allow the Trump administration to withhold records from those same Trump-linked businesses, so long as the communications in question involve presidential decisionmaking. Recent polling shows Democrats with a lead in the generic congressional ballot, with Decision Desk HQ's average putting the party ahead of Republicans by roughly 6 points , 46% to 40%, a margin Democrats have held since April. 🚨BREAKING NEWS — top of @PunchbowlNews DOJ office of legal counsel has issued an opinion that would allow the president to claim executive privilege over communication between him and “private advisors.” Extends to “direct advisors” communication with outside advisers.
